summary: Aurora Motion operates connected electric transit across 31 cities. This annual review follows the network's expansion, operating discipline, and the priorities riders identified for the year ahead.
headline: Cleaner routes. Stronger access. Shared progress.
performance_summary: Aurora Motion increased route availability while improving operating margin and free-cash-flow conversion. Higher fleet utilization, renewable charging and membership retention strengthened unit economics.
rows: Morning frequency and membership retention exceeded plan.
Late-hour service gained share among hospital commuters.
New charging hubs improved coastal fleet availability.
The second cross-border market reached break-even.
Employer mobility plans increased weekday demand.
Membership bundles lifted retention and trip frequency.
Lighting and station upgrades supported evening travel.
Fleet deployment timing created a small planned decline.
survey_intro: Aurora Motion uses rider feedback to decide where its connected electric fleet should travel, charge and operate next.
attachment_description: Source data for the fictional Aurora Motion performance review
scale_copy: 31 cities connected through a reliable electric transit network.
trust_copy: A 4.9 app rating and membership growth strengthened rider loyalty.
horizon_copy: The next milestone is renewable charging across every depot.
operating_signal: Utilization improved while net leverage declined to 1.5x.
driver_left_copy: Seven expanded markets shortened wait times and improved peak availability. Membership growth followed without relying on broad discounts.
driver_right_copy: Energy per trip fell 16% while renewable coverage reached 94%. The savings funded charging resilience and station safety.
portfolio_summary: Eight transit programs converted local operating insight into repeatable growth. Seven expanded through stronger frequency and retention; Green Avenue absorbed a modest deployment delay.
portfolio_read: Seven programs expanded; one market absorbed a planned deployment delay.
